findings: The eligibility track reached its answer and it is a recorded failure: both extractors failed every type blind; the owner's blind re-reading corrected 108 of 215 items; an independent second reader agreed on 357 of 400 pairs, bootstrap lower bound 0.8475 against a 0.90 bar, so a one-reader reference is not shown adequate to judge an extractor
Anchoring in the re-reading was tested and not supported: every reading was locked before its own reveal, and agreement with the extractors falls across the session where drift would raise it
No learning curve in the reference: correction and disagreement rates are flat across the annotation order, which rules out repairing it by redoing the early trials

The ledger's blind gate rejected a wrong entry: the second-annotation result was first recorded as checked_blind, but the values were seen on 12 November and the plan locked on 13 November; reader blinding and dataset blindness are now distinguished

A handoff paragraph asserted work that did not exist: HANDOFF.md item 3 described the extended acceptance rule as locked and committed, none of it was on main, and the web-editor commit message described work its diff did not contain

Three extractor v1.1 defects recorded with no effect on the current sample: '/>' and '/<' read as strict and five further forms dropped, none occurring in the 216 items; a bare 'WNL' missed; a true multi-cohort trial returning the first value only
